input: Correlate meter temperature spikes with high electrical load draw to detect dangerous loose meter socket jaws or impending meter fires.
expected_output:
### 1. Executive Summary
**High-resolution AMI telemetry correlation indicates critical thermal runaway on meter socket assemblies driven by severe $I^2R$ Joule heating under high load current. Meter `MTR-NY-84920` exhibited internal temperatures reaching 98.4°C (peaking at 102.1°C) at 77.5 A line current, exceeding safe operating thresholds by +88.5°C over expected dissipation baselines. This signature confirms compromised spring-clip tension and loose socket jaws, presenting an immediate structural flashover and fire hazard requiring emergency isolation.**

---

### 2. Telemetry & Thermal Correlation Analytics

```
========================================================================================
THERMAL IMPEDANCE & JOULE HEATING CORRELATION MODEL
Feeder: FD-104-B | Substation: SUB-NORTH-02 | Form: 2S / Residential 200A-400A
Physical Formula: ΔT = (T_internal - T_ambient) ∝ I_rms² × R_contact
========================================================================================
```

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Meter Internal Temperature (`MTR-NY-84920`)** | 98.4 °C (209.1 °F) | ≤ 55.0 °C (at peak load) | +78.9% | **Critical** |
| **Temperature Rise over Ambient ($\Delta T$)** | 67.2 °C | ≤ 18.0 °C | +273.3% | **Critical** |
| **Estimated Contact Resistance ($R_{contact}$)** | 11.2 mΩ | ≤ 1.8 mΩ | +522.2% | **Critical** |
| **Active Load Draw / Current ($I_{rms}$)** | 18.6 kW / 77.5 A | 8.5 kW / 35.4 A (Avg) | +118.8% | **Warning** |
| **Rate of Thermal Rise ($dT/dt$)** | +1.85 °C/min | ≤ 0.35 °C/min | +428.6% | **Critical** |
| **Thermal Dissipation Factor ($Z_{th} = \Delta T / I^2$)** | $1.12 \times 10^{-2} \text{ K/A}^2$ | $\le 2.90 \times 10^{-3} \text{ K/A}^2$ | +286.2% | **Critical** |
| **Peer Meter Average Temp (`FD-104-B` Cohort)** | 48.2 °C | 46.5 °C | +3.6% | **Normal** |

---

### 3. Visualization Trigger

**Recommended Visualization:** Time-Series Multi-Axis Line Chart (Internal Temperature vs. Load Current & Peer Baseline).

input: What is the catastrophic meter melt and residential structure fire risk score across aging socket installations?
expected_output:
### Executive Summary
**Across aging meter socket installations (>30 years old), the Catastrophic Meter Melt and Residential Structure Fire Risk Score has reached an acute elevated level of 88.4 / 100 in legacy residential zones due to spring-jaw mechanical fatigue and high-resistance electrical connections under peak summer load. Over 1,240 smart meters deployed in pre-1980 socket bases exhibit sustained internal temperatures exceeding the 85.0°C safety threshold, signaling imminent thermal runaway and enclosure degradation. Targeted immediate field inspection and AMI continuous temperature polling (5-minute VEE interval) are mandatory to mitigate localized structural fire risks.**

---

### Quantitative Risk & Telemetry Assessment

The composite risk score integrates internal thermistor telemetry ($T_{int}$), rate-of-rise ($dT/dt$), estimated socket jaw contact resistance ($R_{contact} \propto \frac{\Delta T}{I^2}$), and socket enclosure age cohort.

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Composite Fire Risk Score (Pre-1980 Sockets)** | 88.4 / 100 | < 25.0 / 100 | +253.6% | **Critical** |
| **Composite Fire Risk Score (1980–1994 Sockets)** | 71.2 / 100 | < 25.0 / 100 | +184.8% | **Warning** |
| **Peak AMI Internal Temperature ($T_{max}$)** | 96.8°C | ≤ 65.0°C (ANSI C12.1) | +48.9% | **Critical** |
| **Mean Thermal Rise Rate ($dT/dt$)** | 4.8°C / hr | ≤ 1.2°C / hr | +300.0% | **Critical** |
| **Estimated Socket Jaw Resistance ($R_{jaw}$)** | 18.7 mΩ | ≤ 2.5 mΩ | +648.0% | **Critical** |
| **High-Risk Endpoints ($T_{int} \ge 85^\circ\text{C}$)** | 1,240 Units | 0 Units | N/A | **Critical** |
| **Interval VEE Temperature Telemetry Success** | 99.82% | ≥ 99.50% | +0.32% | **Normal** |

---

### Risk Distribution Visualization

```json
{
  "chart_type": "bar",
  "title": "Catastrophic Meter Melt & Fire Risk Score by Socket Vintage Cohort",
  "categories": [
    "Pre-1980 (40+ yrs)",
    "1980-1994 (30-40 yrs)",
    "1995-2004 (20-30 yrs)",
    "2005-2014 (10-20 yrs)",
    "2015-Present (<10 yrs)"
  ],
  "series": [
    {
      "name": "Mean Risk Score (0-100)",
      "data": [88.4, 71.2, 43.6, 22.1, 8.5]
    },
    {
      "name": "Peak Internal Temp (°C)",
      "data": [96.8, 84.5, 68.2, 54.0, 42.3]
    },
    {
      "name": "Jaw Resistance (mΩ)",
      "data": [18.7, 12.4, 6.8, 2.9, 1.1]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### Root Cause Analysis & Engineering Observations
1. **Mechanical Jaw Tension Loss**: Thermal cycling over 30+ operational years has relaxed the spring tension in legacy residential bypass/non-bypass meter socket jaws, increasing micro-arcing and contact resistance from nominal (<2 mΩ) to >18 mΩ.
2. **Joule Heating ($I^2R$) Coupling**: Under high air conditioning load (40A–60A continuous), contact points dissipate excess localized heat (30W–65W per jaw), driving base polycarbonate enclosure melting and terminal lug degradation.
3. **Thermal Runaway Threshold**: Telemetry demonstrates that once meter internal thermistors sustain $>85.0^\circ\text{C}$ with an ambient delta $>40.0^\circ\text{C}$, the rate of thermal acceleration triples, posing an immediate flashover/melt hazard.

---

### Actionable Recommendations

1. **High-Frequency AMI Polling**: Switch all endpoints identified in the Pre-1980 and 1980–1994 cohorts exhibiting $T_{int} > 75^\circ\text{C}$ to 5-minute autonomous temperature trap alerts via the AMI mesh network.
2. **Targeted Socket Remediation Program**: Prioritize physical socket box replacements for the 1,240 flagged meters exhibiting $T_{int} \ge 85^\circ\text{C}$.
3. **Cross-Domain Escalation**: Escalate high-risk feeders to the Work Management and Asset Inspection Agent for thermographic infrared (IR) aerial/ground verification.

---
